question: What do the four static OptionTypeInfo maps used by the TTL family hold -- the maps whose addresses merged PR #4065 records only as globals (0x6509440, 0x65093c0, 0x6509400, 0x6509480) without pinning their entries?

open_unknowns: the contents of the four TTL OptionTypeInfo maps
resolves.answer: The static initializer 0x6206ef0 inserts exactly one entry into each of the four maps: 'user_operator' into 0x6509480, 'ttl' into 0x6509440, 'user_filter_factory' into 0x6509400 and 'user_filter' into 0x65093c0. All four entries carry type 22; three carry verification 1 and flags 0x400, while 'user_filter_factory' carries verification 3 and flags 0x400, and 'user_filter' carries verification 1 and flags 0x1200. The 'ttl' entry reuses the preceding block's pack and flags: its block sets neither of its own. A fifth map, 0x65094c0, is zeroed and atexit-registered by the initializer but receives no insert there.

blocks.pack_source: inherited from the preceding block: the ttl block sets no pack/flags of its own

0x65094c0.note: zeroed at the initializer entry (0x6206ef5) and atexit-registered; no insert into this map in the initializer 0x6206ef0

consumers.note: The maps are the option maps of the TTL family, consumed by the ctors' RegisterOptions calls. The ctors, their groups and the maps' addresses are pinned by merged PR #4065; the runtime methods and vtables by merged PR #4087. This packet pins only the maps' contents, which neither packet records.

groups.used_by: filter ctor 0x6202a10 (site 0x6202aa4) and factory ctor 0x6205790 (site 0x6205895), per #4065
